Colombia's corporate rate, where essentially all operating income arises. The reported FY2025 effective rate of 61.7% ($127.7m on $207.1m) is NOT a usable forward rate: it is inflated by non-deductible fair-value losses on financial instruments, unrecorded deferred tax assets and foreign exchange. The Canadian statutory rate of 27% disclosed in the tax note is the parent's rate, not the rate on Colombian mining profit. 35% is the defensible normalised rate; it is sensitised in the scenario set.

The new Bulk Mining Zone and CIP plant reach first gold in Q4 2026, ramping to a stated steady-state run-rate of ~200koz per year. The ramp shape between first gold and steady state is an analyst judgement; the 200koz destination is the company's published target.

Full-year 2026 guidance range is 35%-40%; H1 2026 delivered 43%. The midpoint of guidance (38%) is used rather than the H1 outturn, because the H1 result was helped by an exceptionally high gold price and management has not raised the guide. CMP AISC per ounce = realised gold price x (1 - margin), so CMP costs scale with the gold price and the CMP stream contributes far less price leverage than Owner Mining. This is the single most important structural feature of the model.
